title: Single-module base change under the top-open isomorphism
statement: Let $p:Y\to B$ and $g:A\to B$ be morphisms of schemes, $M$ a sheaf of modules on $Y$, $j:Y|_\top\to Y$ the top-open inclusion and $N=j^*M$ its ordinary restriction. Use the standard derived categories and the canonical single-module comparison $\beta(p,M,g)$ of [def-pc-standard-single-base-change-map]. There exist isomorphisms $e:Rp_*(M[0])\simeq R(pj)_*(N[0])$ on $B$ and $t:R\operatorname{pr}_{A,*}((\operatorname{pr}_{Y|_\top}^*N)[0])\simeq R\operatorname{pr}_{A,*}((\operatorname{pr}_Y^*M)[0])$ on $A$, where the two fibre products are $(Y|_\top)\times_B A$ and $Y\times_B A$ respectively, such that $\beta(p,M,g)=Lg^*(e)\circ\beta(pj,N,g)\circ t$ in left-to-right composition order. In particular the source comparison is an isomorphism before applying $Lg^*$, not an arbitrary isomorphism between the pulled-back objects. No quasi-coherence, relative flatness, quasi-compactness or affineness is assumed.

source.place: cohomology.tex, Tag 08HY (Remark, base-change counit construction); Tag 0D5S (Lemma, composition of derived pullback)

proof.text: The top-open inclusion j is an isomorphism. Its exact restriction agrees with tensor pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. On single complexes, the pinned derived counit and the single comparison therefore give an isomorphism alpha:Lj*(M[0]) to N[0]. The composition and identity comparisons exhibit Lj* as an equivalence, so its pinned derived adjunction unit is invertible. Compose Rp_* of this unit, the inverse right-adjoint mate of the pullback composition comparison for j,p, and R(pj)_* of alpha. This constructs e on B before applying Lg*.

Apply the source-open unit naturality equation to U=top, K=M[0], Kprime=(pr_Y^*M)[0], and phi the pinned single pullback map. Both inserted units are invertible, since j and its base change are isomorphisms. The single pullback composition equation identifies the restricted coefficient arrow with the ordinary pullback of N, after the canonical tensor composition isomorphisms. This substitutes alpha into the source and gives the corresponding single target isomorphism. Use the apex-isomorphism comparison to identify the iterated pullback in the source-open equation with the canonical pullback of pj and g. Compose the resulting target comparisons inversely to obtain t. The source-open equation then reads beta(p,M,g)=Lg*(e);beta(pj,N,g);t. Naturality, inverse cancellation and associativity justify this reassociation. This construction also applies to empty schemes and zero modules.

lean.statement:
theorem standardSingleBaseChange_topRestriction_comparison
    {Y B A : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ B) (M : Y.Modules) (g : A ⟶ B) :
    letI := fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    let j := (⊤ : Y.Opens).ι
    let N := M.restrict j
    ∃ (e : (schemeDerivedDirectImage p).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M) ≅
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage (j ≫ p)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N))
      (t : (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd (j ≫ p) g)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj (pullback.fst (j ≫ p) g) N)) ≅
        (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd p g)).obj
          ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
            (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj (pullback.fst p g) M))),
      standardSingleBaseChangeMap p M g =
        (derivedPullback g).map e.hom ≫
          standardSingleBaseChangeMap (j ≫ p) N g ≫ t.hom
